name: What unexpected issues commonly arise when remodeling bathrooms in older Denver-area homes?

mainEntity.name: What unexpected issues commonly arise when remodeling bathrooms in older Denver-area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in established Denver neighborhoods often hide galvanized steel pipes, ungrounded wiring, degraded cast iron drains, and uneven framing behind plaster or lath. When gutting an older bathroom, you must often level settled subfloors before laying new tile to prevent cracking. Updating outdated plumbing to modern PEX and PVC ensures reliable water pressure and prevents concealed leaks. Planning for potential structural adjustments and mechanical upgrades behind the walls helps you set a realistic contingency plan during renovations in mature properties.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes often have deteriorated galvanized plumbing, ungrounded electrical, uneven subfloors, and plaster walls that require modern reinforcement.
